subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 16, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - October 16, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS community,

As we continue to push forward with our mission to create a user-friendly, privacy-focused Linux distribution, we're excited to share some updates from the past week. Our community has been actively contributing to the project, and we're grateful for their efforts.

One of the notable developments is the release of acreetion-surf v2.0.0, which marks a significant milestone in our journey. This new version brings improved performance and stability, making it an even more enjoyable experience for our users. We're thrilled to see the positive feedback from our community members who have already started using the new version.

In other news, we've been keeping an eye on the latest developments in the Linux world. A recent article on BetaNews highlights AcreetionOS as an easy-to-use alternative to Windows 10/11. This is a testament to our hard work and dedication to creating a user-friendly distribution that's free from telemetry and other unwanted features.

On a more serious note, we've been monitoring a recent malware threat that's affecting Arch Linux users. Our community has been proactive in spreading awareness about this issue, and we're grateful for their vigilance. As always, we recommend exercising caution when downloading packages from unknown sources.

In other news, Shelly 3.1.7, a GUI package manager for Arch Linux, has added support for RLPM (Rolling Release Package Manager) native package engine. This is an exciting development for our community, as it will make it easier for users to manage packages on their systems.

We're also happy to announce that our community member, cobra3282000, has made significant contributions to the project. Their work on Calamares, the universal Linux installer, has been instrumental in ensuring a smooth user experience for our users. We're grateful for their dedication and expertise.

As we continue to move forward, we're committed to maintaining our core values of user-friendliness, privacy, and community involvement. We're always looking for ways to improve and expand our distribution, and we welcome any suggestions or contributions from our community members.

In the coming weeks, we'll be focusing on further improving our distribution and addressing any issues that may arise. We're excited to see what the future holds for AcreetionOS, and we're grateful for the support of our community.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community. We're proud to have you on board, and we look forward to continuing to work together to create a better Linux distribution for all.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva
Co-Lead Developer, AcreetionOS
